title: A generic Sylow-elimination lemma: order 5·m forces a normal Sylow 5-subgroup
description: The verified Abel–Ruffini proof that x⁵−4x+2 is not solvable by radicals (parent AbelRuffiniOQ04OQ01) rules out |Gal| ∈ {10, 20, 40} with three essentially verbatim private lemmas gal_card_ne_10 / _20 / _40. Each is a Sylow argument on a subgroup G ≤ S₅ of order 5·m (m = 2, 4, 8): the Sylow 5-subgroup has order 5, the count n₅ divides m and is ≡ 1 (mod 5) forcing n₅ = 1, so the Sylow 5-subgroup is normal and equals ⟨c⟩ for any order-5 element c; only the final 'no transposition normalizes a 5-cycle' step is specific to S₅. Open question oq-03 asks to factor the shared skeleton — a pure group-theory fact depending solely on the group order — into a single generic lemma parameterized by the order. This entry does exactly that, fully abstractly (no Polynomial.Gal, no permutations, no native_decide): zpowers_order5_normal proves that in ANY finite group of order 5·m with 5 ∤ m and the only divisor d ∣ m with d ≡ 1 (mod 5) being d = 1, the cyclic subgroup generated by any order-5 element is normal; conj_mem_zpowers_order5 is the immediate corollary that every element normalizes ⟨c⟩. The three original orders 10 = 5·2, 20 = 5·4, 40 = 5·8 are recovered as examples discharging the divisor hypothesis for m ∈ {2, 4, 8}.

meta.author: Sylow / classical; Lean formalization original (researcher-7)
meta.assumptions: None. Machine-checked with 0 axioms and 0 sorries (foundational propext/Classical.choice/Quot.sound only; no native_decide, unlike the private lemmas it factors which used native_decide for the concrete Sylow-order computation). Builds on Mathlib's Sylow API: Sylow.nonempty, Sylow.card_eq_multiplicity, card_sylow_modEq_one, Sylow.card_dvd_index, Sylow.smul_eq_iff_mem_normalizer, IsPGroup.exists_le_sylow, together with Nat.factorization_mul / Nat.factorization_eq_zero_of_not_dvd and Nat.card_zpowers.

originalContributions: zpowers_order5_normal: for any finite group G with Nat.card G = 5·m, 5 ∤ m, and (∀ d ∣ m, d ≡ 1 mod 5 → d = 1), the subgroup ⟨c⟩ generated by any order-5 element c is normal — the shared group-theoretic core of the three verbatim lemmas gal_card_ne_10/_20/_40, lifted to an arbitrary group and parameterized by the order.
conj_mem_zpowers_order5: the corollary that under those hypotheses every g satisfies g·c·g⁻¹ ∈ ⟨c⟩ — the exact 'hconj_zpow' step reused in all three original lemmas.

A native_decide-free proof of the Sylow-order computation (order 5·m has Sylow 5-subgroup of order exactly 5) via Nat.factorization_mul, replacing the concrete native_decide calls of the private lemmas and yielding a 0-axiom result.
Explicit examples verifying the divisor hypothesis for m ∈ {2, 4, 8}, recovering the three original orders 10, 20, 40 from the single generic lemma.
zpowers_le_center_of_coprime_index: promotes the single-element centrality criterion mem_center_of_coprime_index to the whole cyclic Sylow-p subgroup — when the index m is coprime to p−1, ⟨c⟩ ≤ Z(G).
prime_dvd_card_center_of_coprime_index: Lagrange applied to the central subgroup ⟨c⟩ forces p ∣ |Z(G)|, so under coprime index the centre is nontrivial with order a multiple of p.
exists_pComplement: Schur-Zassenhaus (Subgroup.exists_right_complement'_of_coprime) gives a p-complement H of order m to the normal Sylow-p subgroup ⟨c⟩ — needs only p ∤ m.

exists_normal_pComplement_of_coprime_index: when ⟨c⟩ is central the complement H is itself normal (proved via the IsComplement' factorization g = n·h₀ with n central), exhibiting G as the internal direct product ⟨c⟩ × H of its central Sylow-p subgroup and a normal p-complement — the structural endgame of the coprime-index analysis.

overview.historicalContext: In the classical proof that a specific quintic such as x⁵ − 4x + 2 is not solvable by radicals, one computes its Galois group over ℚ and shows it is the full symmetric group S₅. A key step eliminates the intermediate possibilities |Gal| ∈ {10, 20, 40}. All three are handled by the same Sylow argument: a transitive subgroup of S₅ of order 5·m (m = 2, 4, 8) has a unique — hence normal — Sylow 5-subgroup, generated by a 5-cycle, which no transposition can normalize. In the formalized proof these appeared as three nearly identical private lemmas. Sylow's theorems (1872) are exactly the tool that makes the uniqueness argument uniform across the three orders, since in each case the number of Sylow 5-subgroups n₅ divides the 5′-part m and satisfies n₅ ≡ 1 (mod 5), whose only common solution is n₅ = 1.
overview.problemStatement: Factor the three verbatim Sylow-elimination lemmas gal_card_ne_10 / _20 / _40 — which differ only in the group order 10, 20, 40 — into a single generic lemma parameterized by the order. Isolate the pure group-theoretic content (independent of the symmetric group and of Galois theory): in a finite group of order 5·m with 5 ∤ m and no divisor d of m with d ≡ 1 (mod 5) other than 1, the cyclic subgroup generated by any order-5 element is normal.
overview.proofStrategy: Let G be finite with Nat.card G = 5·m, 5 ∤ m. (1) Order of the Sylow 5-subgroup: Sylow.card_eq_multiplicity gives |P₅| = 5^(v₅(|G|)); since |G| = 5·m and 5 ∤ m, Nat.factorization_mul plus Nat.factorization_eq_zero_of_not_dvd give v₅(5·m) = 1, so |P₅| = 5 (no native_decide needed). (2) Uniqueness: the index of P₅ is m (from index·|P₅| = |G|), and card_sylow_modEq_one together with Sylow.card_dvd_index give n₅ ∣ m and n₅ ≡ 1 (mod 5); the divisor hypothesis huniq forces n₅ = 1. (3) Normality: a unique Sylow subgroup is normal — Subsingleton (Sylow 5 G) and Sylow.smul_eq_iff_mem_normalizer show every element lies in the normalizer. (4) Identification with ⟨c⟩: for an order-5 element c, IsPGroup.exists_le_sylow places ⟨c⟩ inside a Sylow subgroup, which by uniqueness is P₅; a cardinality-matching bijection (both have order 5) gives P₅ = ⟨c⟩. Transporting normality along this equality yields (⟨c⟩).Normal. The corollary conj_mem_zpowers_order5 is then Normal.conj_mem.
keyInsights: The three orders 10, 20, 40 differ only in the 5′-part m ∈ {2, 4, 8}; every other line of the three original lemmas is byte-for-byte identical. The right abstraction is therefore a lemma quantified over the group order 5·m, with the arithmetic that varies (which divisors of m are ≡ 1 mod 5) packaged as a single hypothesis huniq.

Uniqueness of the Sylow 5-subgroup, not its explicit description, is what delivers normality; Sylow's third theorem (n₅ ∣ m and n₅ ≡ 1 mod 5) is exactly the mechanism that turns a statement about the order into n₅ = 1 for all three m simultaneously.

The divisibility hypothesis in huniq is genuinely needed for m = 8: the divisor 6 satisfies 6 ≡ 1 (mod 5), and only 6 ∤ 8 rules it out. The congruence alone does not suffice — this is why huniq takes both d ∣ m and d % 5 = 1.

Abstracting away from S₅ eliminates the concrete native_decide calls used in the private lemmas to compute the Sylow order; the arithmetic v₅(5·m) = 1 is proved symbolically via Nat.factorization_mul, making the generic lemma 0-axiom where the specializations were not.

Normality of ⟨c⟩ is only the entry point: the N/C theorem ([G : C_G(c)] ∣ p − 1) plus the class equation turn 'the Sylow subgroup is normal' into a full structural classification. When the index m is coprime to p − 1 the element c becomes central, yielding a normal p-complement and hence an internal direct product G ≅ ⟨c⟩ × H — and from there solvability (for m a prime power), the sharp upgrade to nilpotency (in the coprime regime), and the classical facts that every group of order 15, 33, or 35 is cyclic all follow. The Abel–Ruffini orders 20 and 40 sit precisely on the non-coprime side, the exact boundary where nilpotency fails while solvability survives.
prerequisites: Sylow's theorems: existence, conjugacy, and the count n_p ≡ 1 (mod p) with n_p dividing the index

p-groups and the fact that every p-subgroup lies in a Sylow p-subgroup

sections.title: Framing and Setup
sections.summary: Module docstring: the verified Abel–Ruffini x⁵−4x+2 proof rules out |Gal| ∈ {10, 20, 40} with three verbatim private lemmas gal_card_ne_10/_20/_40, each a Sylow argument on a subgroup of order 5·m. This file factors that shared core into one generic lemma and lifts it from the fixed prime 5 to an arbitrary prime p — a genuine generalization (the mod-p and cancellation steps that omega/interval_cases dispatch on numerals now need Nat.mod_eq_of_lt and Nat.eq_of_mul_eq_mul_right). Fully abstract, native_decide-free, 0-sorry/0-axiom. `import Mathlib`; `namespace AbelRuffiniSylowElim`; `open scoped Classical`.
sections.mathContext: $|G| = pm,\ p \nmid m,\ (\forall d \mid m,\ d \equiv 1\ (\mathrm{mod}\ p) \Rightarrow d = 1).$

sections.title: Section 1 — the generic Sylow-elimination core
sections.summary: zpowers_sylow_normal: in a finite group of order p·m with p ∤ m and no divisor d ∣ m with d ≡ 1 (mod p) other than d = 1, the Sylow p-subgroup is unique — hence normal — and equals ⟨c⟩ for any order-p element c, so ⟨c⟩ ⊴ G. Uses the p-part of |G| = p·m (Nat.factorization), Sylow's third theorem (card_sylow_modEq_one, Sylow.card_dvd_index) forcing nₚ = 1, and a cardinality bijection to identify Pₚ = ⟨c⟩. conj_mem_zpowers_sylow: consequently every g normalizes ⟨c⟩. involution_conj_eq_self_or_inv: conjugation by an involution fixes or inverts c.
sections.mathContext: $P_p$ unique $\Rightarrow P_p = \langle c\rangle \trianglelefteq G$; every $g$ normalizes $\langle c\rangle$.

sections.title: Section 2 — from involutions to arbitrary automorphism order
sections.summary: conj_pow_eq_zpow_pow and conj_exponent_pow_modEq_one lift the involution computation to conjugation by an element of arbitrary order: the induced automorphism of ⟨c⟩ ≅ ℤ/p is an integer power, and its order divides p − 1 (the order of Aut(ℤ/p) = (ℤ/p)ˣ), giving the modular relation that drives the N/C bound.
sections.mathContext: $g c g^{-1} = c^{k}$ with $k^{e} \equiv 1\ (\mathrm{mod}\ p)$, $e \mid p-1$.

sections.title: Section 3 — the N/C bound: centralizer index divides p − 1
sections.summary: conjNormal_ker_eq_centralizer identifies the kernel of the conjugation action on the normal ⟨c⟩ with the centralizer of c; conjNormal_ker_index_dvd_sub_one and centralizer_index_dvd_sub_one then give [G : C_G(c)] ∣ p − 1 (the N/C theorem: G/C embeds in Aut(⟨c⟩) of order p − 1). huniq_of_lt discharges the divisor side-condition for m < p.

sections.title: Section 4 — structural consequence: the group is not simple
sections.summary: zpowers_index_eq computes [G : ⟨c⟩] = m, and not_isSimpleGroup_of_sylow concludes G is not simple: the proper nontrivial normal subgroup ⟨c⟩ obstructs simplicity whenever 1 < m, the abstract form of 'S₅ has a proper normal 5-subgroup here' that powered the original elimination.
sections.mathContext: $1 < m \Rightarrow \langle c\rangle$ a proper nontrivial normal subgroup $\Rightarrow G$ not simple.

sections.title: Section 5 — conjugacy-class size and coprime-index centrality
sections.summary: The conjugacy-class-size form of the N/C bound: orbit_conjAct_card_eq_centralizer_index and conjClass_card_dvd_sub_one give |cl(c)| ∣ p − 1, while zpowers_le_centralizer, centralizer_index_dvd_index_zpowers and conjClass_card_dvd_gcd sharpen this to |cl(c)| ∣ gcd(m, p − 1). mem_center_of_coprime_index: if gcd(m, p − 1) = 1 then |cl(c)| = 1, i.e. c is central.

sections.title: Section 6 — central Sylow, p ∣ |Z(G)|, and the normal p-complement
sections.summary: In the coprime regime: zpowers_le_center_of_coprime_index puts ⟨c⟩ ≤ Z(G) and prime_dvd_card_center_of_coprime_index gives p ∣ |Z(G)|. exists_pComplement and exists_normal_pComplement_of_coprime_index produce a (normal) p-complement H with |H| = m and G = ⟨c⟩ ⋉ H — the structural skeleton of the internal direct-product decomposition proved later.
sections.mathContext: $\langle c\rangle \le Z(G),\ p \mid |Z(G)|,\ \exists H \trianglelefteq G,\ |H| = m,\ \langle c\rangle \cap H = 1.$

sections.title: Section 7 — the fixed prime p = 5 and the orders 10, 20, 40
sections.summary: The p = 5 specialisations recovering the Abel–Ruffini inputs as one-liners: zpowers_order5_normal, conj_mem_zpowers_order5, not_isSimpleGroup_order5, mem_center_order5_of_coprime_index. The 'Recovering the three original orders' block instantiates m ∈ {2, 4, 8} to give |G| ∈ {10, 20, 40}; the m = 8 case highlights that 6 ≡ 1 (mod 5) is harmless only because 6 ∤ 8.
sections.mathContext: $m \in \{2, 4, 8\} \leftrightarrow |G| \in \{10, 20, 40\}$ — the divisor hypothesis holds in each case.

sections.title: Section 8 — solvability when the index is a prime power
sections.summary: isSolvable_zpowers (abelian ⟨c⟩ is solvable) and isSolvable_of_normal_solvable_quotient combine with the normal p-complement so that isSolvable_of_sylow_primePow_index proves G solvable whenever m = qᵏ: G is an extension of the solvable p-complement by the abelian ⟨c⟩. isSolvable_order5_primePow_index is the p = 5 form.
sections.mathContext: $m = q^{k} \Rightarrow G$ solvable (extension of solvable $H$ by abelian $\langle c\rangle$).

sections.title: Section 9 — the sharp strengthening: nilpotency in the coprime regime
sections.summary: isNilpotent_of_sylow_central_primePow_index: in the coprime regime gcd(qᵏ, p − 1) = 1 the central Sylow p-subgroup makes G nilpotent, not merely solvable — a strictly stronger conclusion. isNilpotent_order5_central_primePow_index is the p = 5 form. The Abel–Ruffini orders 20, 40 sit on the non-coprime side (F₂₀ is solvable but not nilpotent), pinpointing exactly where the strengthening fails.
sections.mathContext: $\gcd(q^{k}, p-1) = 1 \Rightarrow G$ nilpotent; e.g. $F_{20}$ (non-coprime) is solvable but not nilpotent.

sections.title: Section 10 — central Sylow to abelian, and cyclicity of order 15
sections.summary: The G ⧸ ⟨c⟩ cyclic upgrade: zpowers_normal_of_mem_center, mul_comm_of_center_zpowers_cyclic_quotient and isCyclic_quotient_zpowers_of_prime_index show that a central ⟨c⟩ with cyclic prime-index quotient forces G abelian (mul_comm_of_prime_index_coprime, mul_comm_of_card_fifteen). isCyclic_of_comm_card_eq_prime_mul_prime and isCyclic_of_card_fifteen conclude that every group of order 15 is cyclic.
sections.mathContext: $Z \supseteq \langle c\rangle,\ G/\langle c\rangle$ cyclic $\Rightarrow G$ abelian; $|G| = 15 \Rightarrow G \cong \mathbb{Z}/15$.

sections.title: Section 11 — the general order-pq classification and its converse
sections.summary: The positive half and its sharp converse: mul_comm_of_card_eq_prime_mul_prime_of_not_dvd and isCyclic_of_card_eq_prime_mul_prime_of_not_dvd give that a group of order p·q with p ∤ (q − 1) (and q ∤ (p − 1)) is cyclic, while dvd_sub_one_of_not_isCyclic_card_eq_prime_mul_prime is the converse. isCyclic_of_card_thirtyfive (35) and isCyclic_of_card_thirtythree (33) are concrete instances.
sections.mathContext: $|G| = pq,\ p \nmid q-1 \Rightarrow G$ cyclic; e.g. orders $15, 33, 35$.

sections.title: Section 12 — the internal direct product G ≃* ⟨c⟩ × H
sections.summary: The structural endgame: exists_mulEquiv_prod_zpowers_of_coprime_index upgrades the semidirect-product data to a genuine isomorphism G ≃* ⟨c⟩ × H, specialised in exists_mulEquiv_prod_of_card_fifteen. exists_pComplement_isCyclic_iff / _isNilpotent_iff (and their order-15 forms) characterise exactly when the complement — hence G — is cyclic or nilpotent, closing the classification.
sections.mathContext: $G \cong \langle c\rangle \times H$ (coprime central regime); complement cyclic/nilpotent $\iff G$ is.

conclusion.summary: The three verbatim private lemmas gal_card_ne_10 / _20 / _40 of the Abel–Ruffini x⁵−4x+2 proof are factored into one generic, fully abstract lemma: in any finite group of order 5·m with 5 ∤ m and no divisor d ∣ m with d ≡ 1 (mod 5) except d = 1, the cyclic subgroup generated by any order-5 element is normal (zpowers_order5_normal), and consequently every element normalizes it (conj_mem_zpowers_order5). The orders 10, 20, 40 are the m ∈ {2, 4, 8} instances. Follow-up OQ04·OQ01·OQ03·OQ01 lifts this core from the fixed prime 5 to an arbitrary prime p (zpowers_sylow_normal / conj_mem_zpowers_sylow); the fixed-5 lemma zpowers_order5_normal is now a one-line corollary. Generalizing the prime is not cosmetic: variable p forces Nat.mod_eq_of_lt (to evaluate 1 % p) and Nat.eq_of_mul_eq_mul_right (nonlinear index cancellation [G:P]·p = p·m), steps that omega/interval_cases discharge automatically only for the concrete numeral 5.
conclusion.significance: Replaces three near-duplicate Sylow arguments with a single reusable group-theory lemma parameterized by the group order, isolating the content that is independent of the symmetric group and of Galois theory. The abstraction also removes the native_decide calls of the specializations, so the generic core is 0-axiom verified.
implications: Any order-5-cycle normality argument in a group of order 5·m (with the divisor condition) now reduces to a single lemma application, as the three original orders demonstrate.

Provides exactly the 'g normalizes ⟨c⟩' input that the S₅-specific 'no transposition normalizes a 5-cycle' step consumes, cleanly separating the group-order arithmetic from the permutation-theoretic contradiction.
openQuestions: Generalize from the prime 5 to an arbitrary prime p: in a group of order p·m with p ∤ m and the analogous divisor hypothesis, the subgroup generated by any order-p element is normal.

Replace the divisor hypothesis huniq by the sharper structural condition on m under which a group of order p·m must have a normal Sylow p-subgroup, and characterize exactly which orders 5·m force normality.
